introduction-desktop-vs-application.core: End-user computing delivers work environments from the cloud: WorkSpaces provides persistent virtual desktops (a full Windows or Linux desktop per user), while AppStream 2.0 streams individual applications from non-persistent fleets to a browser. Data stays in AWS, endpoints just display pixels.

first_principles.problem: Contractors need access to sensitive apps without copying data to unmanaged laptops.
truths: Some users need full desktops, others one app.
derivation: **One or a few apps, ephemeral** → AppStream 2.0.

analogy.title: Renting a furnished office versus booking a meeting room
analogy.story: The office is yours with your things; the meeting room is set up fresh each time.
analogy.breaks: Offices are physical; desktops stream as pixels to any device.

example.title: Choosing for two groups
flow: External auditors needing one finance app → AppStream

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Right experience, data never leaves AWS.

check.q: Which service streams individual applications from non-persistent instances?

amazon-workspaces-the-persistent-desktop.core: WorkSpaces gives each user a persistent virtual desktop (Windows or Linux) with a root and user volume, in bundles of CPU/RAM/storage, joined to a directory (AWS Managed AD, AD Connector), billed monthly (AlwaysOn) or hourly (AutoStop). Access via WorkSpaces clients or web over DCV/PCoIP, with optional Pools for non-persistent desktops.

first_principles.problem: Laptop refreshes and VPN bottlenecks make remote onboarding slow and risky.
derivation: Choose **AlwaysOn vs AutoStop** by usage hours.

analogy.title: A personal desk in a remote office tower
analogy.story: Your desk stays as you left it, and you access it from anywhere.
analogy.breaks: Desks don't bill by the hour; AutoStop WorkSpaces do.

check.q: When is AutoStop billing better than AlwaysOn?
check.a: For users who work fewer hours per month, below the break-even point.

amazon-appstream-20-the-ephemeral-stream.core: AppStream 2.0 streams applications from fleets of instances built from an image. Users get a fresh session each time (data in home folders on S3, or persisted via app settings), through a browser with no install. Fleets can be always-on, on-demand or elastic, scaling with demand, and you pay per instance hour plus user fees.

first_principles.problem: A university needs to give 2,000 students access to CAD software for a semester without installing it on their laptops.
truths: Many users need only specific apps.
Fresh sessions reduce drift and risk.
derivation: Create a **stack** with user settings and storage.

analogy.title: Streaming a film instead of buying the DVD
analogy.story: You get it instantly in a browser, and nothing stays on your device.
analogy.breaks: Films are watched passively; apps need GPU and input latency tuning.

example.title: Semester CAD access
flow: Image with CAD on GPU instance type

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Students run CAD from any laptop.

check.q: What's the difference between AppStream fleet types always-on and on-demand?
check.a: Always-on instances run continuously for instant sessions; on-demand instances are stopped until users connect, saving cost with a short start delay.

vdi-patterns-in-the-cloud.core: Common cloud VDI patterns: persistent desktops for knowledge workers, non-persistent pools for task workers, app streaming for contractors and BYOD, GPU desktops for graphics, and secure enclaves for regulated data. Design considerations include identity integration, network latency to users (region choice), data controls, golden image management and cost by usage pattern.

first_principles.problem: A one-size VDI rollout gives everyone expensive persistent desktops, and latency-sensitive users complain.

analogy.title: Office space planning
analogy.story: Private offices, hot desks, meeting rooms and secure labs, assigned by role.
analogy.breaks: Office space is slow to change; VDI capacity changes in minutes.

check.q: Why choose a region close to VDI users?
check.a: Pixel streaming is latency-sensitive; distance directly affects responsiveness.
